newsitem.title: UK: Calortex claims 38,000 gas customers in U.K. pilot.
newsitem.headline: Calortex claims 38,000 gas customers in U.K. pilot.

text.p: On the day U.K. gas regulator Ofgas delayed the introduction of the second phase of domestic gas competition in England, a participant in the first phase spoke of his satisfaction at the progress of the experiment.

Speaking at a conference on Tuesday, six months to the day after the introduction of the first pilot scheme covering Devon, Cornwall and Somerset in the southwest, Peter Franklin, joint general manager of Calortex, said his company had signed up 38,000 customers at the last count.
He challenged the figure of 75,000 domestic customers said to have switched from British Gas Plc to other suppliers, and said his estimate was nearer 90,000.
He put the nine participating companies into three groups. In the first he saw Calortex and SWEB GAS, each of whom has over 30,000 customers.

In the next block he saw Amerada Hess, Total SA and Eastern Natural Gas, each of which has around 5,000 customers according to his figures. And in the third group, British Fuels Limited, Norweb, Northern and Southern and Phillips have significantly less than this.

Franklin was full of praise for the way in which British Gas and its pipeline arm TransCo have handled the pilot scheme. "It's been a very straightforward and smooth process for us to get contracts started up. British Gas and TransCo should be proud to have done it so well".
But he added that British Gas' share of the market was still too large.
"We haven't yet got the structure for sustainable competition as one supplier is still 10 times bigger than the next biggest. In this respect it is not like the industrial market", he said.
Calortex, a partnership between Calor Group Plc and Texaco Inc, is looking at four key areas to decide how to pursue its aims as the market unfolds.

These are timing, to decide how soon before deregulation to start marketing activities; the mix of advertising, between, for example, television, print media and direct sales; price; and development of a brand name.
"The leaders are not the cheapest at all buyer sizes or all methods of payment, but we are at least competitive", he said.

Emma Stein, managing director of British Fuels Gas, told the conference that while BFL was small in comparison with Calortex, the test of success for her was the cost of each sale, and she was happy that BFL was competitive on this point. Ofgas today deferred the introduction of phase 2 of the pilot in Avon and Dorset to February and Kent and Sussex to March.
